title: Stepper
lead: A fair crash ladder. Ten rungs, cash out any time. Survival to rung k is RTP ÷ payoutₖ, so every stopping rule returns the same 97%: the player chooses variance, never expectation.
figures: examples/ladders.png
Returns, survival and the single-RN crash table for the three difficulties.
examples/strategies.png
Monte Carlo under four stopping rules: every one returns the RTP.
examples/crash.png
Where the crash falls: the eleven slots of the single draw.

title: Single Shot
lead: A single-shot payout function. The field is the 0–10000 draw; zone widths are the probabilities; inside a zone the payout ramps from a − r to a + r. Payouts and RTP in, a monotone payout(u) out, exact by summation.
figures: examples/curves.png
Same payouts, same RTP, same r under three probability assignments. Only the zone widths move.
examples/bands.png
Inside every band the paid multiple is exactly uniform on [a − r, a + r].

title: Top 3
lead: Elo array + one uniform → fair Plackett–Luce ranking → top-3 payout. Strength is 10^(Elo/400); one draw picks the winner and its leftover is recycled to pick second, third and the rest. Win/place/show probabilities are closed-form, and every podium finish returns stake plus profit: second pays a quarter and third a fifth of the win profit, which is solved per racer so every racer returns exactly the RTP.
tags: place terms 1 / ¼ / ⅕, RTP-exact per racer
figures: examples/places.png
Closed-form win / place / show probabilities against the feasibility bound, and the per-racer place-terms multipliers.
examples/sim-place-terms.png
200,000 simulated races with a unit stake on every racer: realised return per racer against the design RTP, and the payout distribution for the favourite and the outsider.

title: Top 1
lead: The same Elo race, one uniform recycled into the full ranking, with only the winner paid. Odds are RTP ÷ P(win) = RTP·W / wᵢ, so a 400-Elo gap is a 10:1 odds ratio and every racer returns exactly the RTP with no feasibility condition.
figures: examples/top1.png
Win probability per racer and the odds that return the RTP.

title: Rip & Rumble
lead: Card packs from two decks. A pack is 5 cards without replacement; per rarity it pays count × value × multiplier(count), an exact hypergeometric sum. Each bet type draws the low deck with the one probability that makes E[win] ÷ cost equal the RTP. Reproduces Math-rippin-rumble-ver4.xlsx.
tags: two buckets, mix solved for RTP
figures: examples/rumble.png
Most likely pack compositions per bucket, and the low-bucket probability per bet type against the simulated return.

title: Game of Three
lead: GO3 / Rock n Smash. Three rocks; a fixed table says how many break (0–3) and pays 5 / 1 / 0.5 / 0; on 2 or 3 a gem fires with a fixed chance and multiplies by 2–10× from a weighted table. RTP is the exact sum over 16 outcomes: 97.07% base, 97.15% boosted. Reproduces Rock n Smash.xlsx.
figures: examples/smash.png
The 16 outcome zones per mode with their probabilities and multiples, against the simulated return.

title: Pick One
lead: An n-way bet with exact RTP. Options own zones of width pᵢ on the draw; backing option j pays RTP ÷ pⱼ on a hit, so every option returns exactly the RTP. Two equal options pay 1.9× at RTP 0.95; three pay 2.85×; five pay 4.75×. Weighted options work the same way.
figures: examples/pick.png
Odds and simulated return for 2, 3, 5 and 8 equal options.
